title: Can Improvements to Mobile Internet Service Help Reduce Digital Inequality? An Empirical Analysis of Education and Overall Data Consumption
authors: Karthik Babu Nattamai Kannan; Eric M. Overby; Sridhar Narasimhan
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption of an unlimited mobile data plan by households in three monthly cohorts (January, February, March 2016 = months 13-15), with PSM-matched late-switcher controls untreated throughout the 17-month window; linear household-month regressions with household FE and calendar-month FE interacted with time-invariant groups (matched-stratum cohort and geography x SES), no covariates, clustered by household (Table 3 cols 1 and 4, Table 4 cols 1 and 4, Table 5 cols 1 and 3, Table 6 col 1) plus unstacked event studies (Figure 4). Callaway-Sant'Anna (csdid) is reported in Appendix Figures A5-A6. CAVEAT: the shipped data are synthetic (README: 'anonymized synthetic datasets representative of the data'), so data_access = synthetic and the paper belongs in data/synthetic_packages.txt; published numbers cannot be reproduced from the package.
design_notes: Household x month panel (months 1-17; months 13-15 = Jan-Mar 2016 switch months). Treatment trt_monthly_ind = on unlimited plan in month t (switches off for ~8% of treated households in the synthetic data). Three analysis samples: PSM early vs late switchers (main; synth_psm_inequality_network/edu.dta), random-forest-link matched (Appendix Table A2), switchers vs non-switchers (Appendix Tables A3, A4, A9; p0-p11 lags). Specification: areg y trt_monthly_ind i.batch_id#i.dte i.geo_social_split#i.dte, absorb(acct_id) vce(cluster acct_id). batch_id = cohort of the treated household and of its matched control (symmetric 48,426/46,428/30,598 per cohort for treated and controls), so batch_id#dte is a time-invariant-group x time FE; geo_social_split = 12 geography x SES cells. Heterogeneity columns add trt x group interactions (trt_geoX*, trt_socioX*, trtX* continuous moderators; Tables 3-9 other columns). Figure 5: sensitivity with inflated outcomes dv_geo_*/dv_ses_* (interactions). Figure 6: psm24 files. Appendix: csdid mt_tot_w / edu_dtotmb_w, ivar(acct_id) time(dt_period_end_int) gvar(trt_min_int) method(reg) with csdid_plot by group 13/14/15 (Figures A5-A6, _02_time_comsuming_code.do lines 80-115); Table A8 random-implementation placebo; Table A11 January cohort only; Table A13 zip3 clustering; Table A14 IHS outcomes.
n_eligible_specs_note: 7 static + 2 event-study main-text specs. Appendix qualifying specs (not counted): Table A2 (RF-matched sample, lines 900/912), A3 (non-switcher controls, event study), A9 (non-switchers static, lines 1124/1136), A13 (zip3 clustering), A14 (IHS outcomes, lines 1309+), A11 (January cohort only: single cohort, not eligible), A12 (full unlimited definition).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: trt_min_int in {13, 14, 15} = January, February, March 2016 switchers (synthetic counts 48,426 / 46,428 / 30,598 households); controls switch in months 19-24, after the window ends (month 17).
never_treated_note: Matched late switchers (trt_min_int 19-24) are untreated in every observed month 1-17 (not-yet-treated within the window; never-treated for estimation purposes).
modern_estimators_named: Callaway-Sant'Anna (csdid, method(reg); Appendix Figures A5-A6, by cohort)

specs.sample_condition: PSM-matched sample: 125,452 early-switcher households (Jan/Feb/Mar 2016 cohorts) and 125,452 late-switcher controls, months 1-17 (4,265,368 household-months in the synthetic file)
specs.reported_location: Table 3, column (1) (column order inferred from code: overall-data models first, education models fourth)
specs.notes: Columns (2)-(3) add trt x geography / trt x SES interactions (not eligible).
specs.treatment_definition: 1 if household i is on the carrier's unlimited mobile data plan in month t; early switchers adopt in month 13, 14 or 15 (Jan/Feb/Mar 2016; cohort variable trt_min_int = batch_id); matched late-switcher controls adopt in months 19-24, outside the 17-month estimation window, so they are untreated throughout. In the synthetic data 10,296 of 125,452 treated households show trt_monthly_ind switching back to 0 in some post-adoption month (drop those post periods per PROTOCOL switch-off rule).
specs.fe: acct_id (absorbed) + batch_id#dte (matched-stratum cohort x month; controls carry their matched treated household's batch_id) + geo_social_split#dte (12 geography x SES groups x month)

data_files_note: README (_00_readme_v3.pdf): 'this package offers anonymized synthetic datasets representative of the data used in the paper ... qualitatively similar results in magnitude and direction'. Original carrier data are proprietary.
software_detail: Stata (areg, reghdfe, csdid, coefplot, estout); csdid originally run in R per code comments
priority_note: Eligible design with complete code, but shipped data are synthetic; real data would be needed from the authors.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Table/column mapping inferred from the output filenames (03_table3_main_results etc.) and the order of eststo calls; verify against the published PDF. Panel structure checked with pandas (250,904 households, months 1-17, cohorts 13/14/15, controls 19-24, batch_id symmetric across treated and controls, 10,296 treated households with treatment switching off). Figure 2/3 blocks (lines 46-170) contain no regressions.
